verdict: Apple grew revenue 5% to $95.4B — a March-quarter record — as Services hit an all-time high of $26.6B and the new iPhone 16e joined the lineup, keeping $24.8B as profit.

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: Apple's flagship smartphone — the iPhone 16 family, joined this quarter by the lower-cost iPhone 16e; up 2% YoY.

segments.name: Mac
segments.note: Mac computers — new M4-powered models lifted sales 7%.

segments.name: iPad
segments.note: iPad tablets — new iPad Air and mini models lifted sales 15%.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod, Apple TV and accessories; down 5% YoY.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, Apple TV+ and licensing — an all-time high, up 12% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Spending to design future products and technologies.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Sales, marketing and day-to-day running costs.

follow100Note: Services is now $27.94 of every $100 Apple takes in, and still growing fastest. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Segments are net sales by product category, as Apple reports them.

takeaways.title: Services hit another record
takeaways.text: Services revenue reached an all-time high of $26.6B, up 12% — it is now 28% of everything Apple sells, and it carries much higher margins than hardware.

takeaways.title: EPS set a March-quarter record
takeaways.text: Diluted earnings per share rose 8% to $1.65, a March-quarter record, and Apple returned $29B to shareholders in the quarter through dividends and buybacks.

takeaways.title: iPad bounced back
takeaways.text: iPad sales jumped 15% to $6.4B on new models, while Wearables, Home and Accessories fell 5% to $7.5B — the only shrinking category.
